specialRules.ruleFull: A warband may never have more Grave Guards than Skeleton Warriors.

The Vampire may take one or more Bloodline abilities when he is created. The first costs the price listed, and every later one twice that. Each time he gains a new skill he may take a Bloodline ability instead of the skill, at double cost.

Ability | Cost | Effect
Red Fury | 30 gc | +1 Attack.
Killing Blow | 30 gc | A natural 6 to hit wounds automatically. The blow may not be parried, but armour and other saves are allowed.
Blood Lust | 50 gc | He is subject to frenzy.
Master Strike | 40 gc | He causes a critical hit on a 5 or 6.
Curse Of The Undead | 50 gc | If he goes out of action, after the battle he heals all of his wounds on a D6 roll of 5+, and then does not roll on the serious injury table.
Strength of the Dragon | 40 gc | +1 Strength.
Gift of Abhorash | 30 gc | The warband's maximum number of warriors rises by one, for good.
Warriors within 6" of the Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own.
The Vampire causes fear.
The Vampire is not affected by psychology and takes no All Alone tests.
The Vampire is not affected by any poison.
The Vampire treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down.

The Vampire summoned every undead warrior of the warband. While he is out of action, roll a Leadership test each round for every undead model in the warband: a model that fails goes out of action too.
The Vampire may start with one or more Bloodline abilities, and may take one later instead of a skill. The abilities and their costs are the warband's Bloodline Abilities rule.

A Wight is not affected by any poison.
A Wight treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down.
A natural 6 on the roll to hit wounds automatically. The blow may not be parried, but armour and other saves are allowed.
A Skeleton Warrior causes fear.
A Skeleton Warrior is not affected by psychology and takes no All Alone tests.

A Skeleton Warrior treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down.
Skeleton Warriors may not run, but may charge normally.
Skeleton Warriors gain no experience.

Grave Guards may not run in their rusted armour, but may charge normally.

flags.what: A Blood Dragon warband needs at least 3 models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported. No henchmen group sizes and no maximum profiles are printed.
The PDF opens with the author's warning that the warband is too powerful and suggests limiting the Vampire to one bloodline ability. It is a note on play, not a rule, and is not imported.
The skill table (p2) prints no Special column, so the warband has no skill group: the Vampire takes Combat, Academic, Strength and Speed, the Wight and the Dreg Combat and Strength.

The Wight (p4) takes our Undead race and the Grave Guard (p6) our Grave Guard race; the Skeleton Warrior (p5) and the Hell Hound (p6) are creatures with no race and no maximum profile. The Dreg (p4) is Human.
The Skeletons' (p5) and Grave Guards' (p6) Slow (they may not run, but may charge normally) is our shared May Not Run, under that name.
The Blood Dragon list's Warhorse (80 gc) and Barding (40 gc) are marked "*Vampire Only". The Undead list has no Warhorse or Barding, and the Blood Dragon list no missile weapons.

The Vampire's Summoner rule is his own (the undead collapse while he is out of action); our skill of that name raises the maximum warband size, which is what his Gift of Abhorash bloodline ability does.

The bloodline abilities are bought at creation, doubled for each later one and in place of a skill later. The template has no way to sell them, so they are the warband's Bloodline Abilities rule with their costs and effects.
Grave Guards are "0-5*", the asterisk the footnote that a warband may never have more Grave Guards than Skeletons: the count is 0-5 and the footnote is the warband's Grave Guards rule.
